title: Two-Ball Alternating Push
description: Advanced handlers push two balls in an alternating rhythm up the court, then two together, building hand independence at speed.

content.objective: Control two balls at speed with independent hands, strengthening the weak hand so both hands can push the ball in transition.
content.setup: Players on the baseline with two balls each, spaced in three lanes.
content.organization: Waves of three; the next wave goes when the previous one reaches half court.
instructions: Dribble both balls at the same time, jogging to half court.
Switch to alternating (one up, one down) and jog to the far baseline.
Return at a faster pace with both balls together.
On the last trip, sprint the alternating rhythm to half court.
Finish with 20 stationary alternating dribbles at knee height.
coachingPoints: Push both balls out in front, not straight down.
Eyes up: count the players ahead of you.
commonMistakes: Slowing down to rescue the weak-hand ball.
Bouncing too hard so the ball comes up above the waist.
content.safety: Wide lanes; a lost ball is left until the wave has passed.
progressions: Add a crossover of both balls at half court.
regressions: Use one ball and one tennis ball held in the other hand.
successCriteria: Full length without losing either ball.
Even height and rhythm on both sides.
content.gameApplication: Players who can push the ball with either hand at speed are much harder to force to one side in transition.
